title: Setup for email tracking and delivery | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Create DNS records for landing pages and email: Connecting a CNAME record allows marketers to host web versions of emails, landing pages, and blogs with consistent branding that improves traffic and conversions, it is highly recommended that you add the CNAMEs to your root domain host for Marketo Engage to host your marketing-focused web assets.
t2: Add the CNAME for landing pages: Add the landing page CNAME to your DNS record, so that [YourLandingPageCNAME] points to the unique account string that is assigned to your landing pages, log in to your domain registrar’s site and enter the landing page CNAME and account string.
t3: Add the CNAME for email tracking links: Add the email CNAME so that [YourEmailCNAME] points to [MktoTrackingLink], which is the default tracking link that Marketo Engage assigned, in the format: [YourEmailCNAME].[YourDomain].com IN CNAME [MktoTrackingLink] For example: pages.abc.com IN CNAME mkto-a0244.com The [MktoTrackingLink] value must be the default branding domain.
t4: Set up DMARC: DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) is an authentication protocol that is used to help organizations protect their domain from unauthorized use, it extends the existing authentication protocols, such as SPF and DKIM, to inform recipient servers about the actions to take if an authentication failure occurs on their domain.
t5: Dedicated IPs and shared pool: If you send mail through Marketo Engage over a dedicated IP and have not implemented a branded return-path (or are not sure if you have), open a ticket with Adobe Support.
t6: Set up MX records for your domain: An MX record allows you to receive mail to the domain that you’re sending email from to process replies and auto-responders, if you’re sending from your corporate domain, it is probably already configured, if not, you can usually set it up to map to your corporate domain MX record.
t7: Outbound IP addresses: Marketo Engage makes an outbound connection to an Internet server on your behalf, your IT organization and some partners/vendors may use allow lists to restrict access to servers, if so, you must provide them with Marketo Engage outbound IP address blocks to add to their allow lists.
t8: Outbound IP address blocks: The following lists cover all Marketo Engage servers that make outbound calls, refer to these lists for configuring an IP allowlist, server, firewall, access control list, security group, or third-party service to receive outgoing connections from Marketo Engage.

title: Design accessible content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Font selection: Use sans-serif fonts, such as Arial, Verdana, Tahoma, Helvetica, or Open Sans, avoid serif, cursive, or decorative fonts in body content, stick to a limited font set for consistency and fallback (for example: font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;).
t2: Ensure visual accessibility: To make sure your content is visually accessible, follow these best practices: Avoid using color-only indicators for important information, use text labels or icons to ensure clarity, optimize your design for mobile and responsive layouts, ensuring buttons are large and properly spaced, regularly test across devices and screen sizes to maintain accessibility.
t3: Use readable format: In the visual design space, use the relevant structure and content components to organize your content in a clear, logical and concise way that is accessible to all, set the options in the Styles pane using structural inheritance best practices, ensure that content follows a logical left-to-right, top-to-bottom flow, use clear, concise language.
t4: Test your content test: To verify the content accessibility, you can use the testing capabilities provided by Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, they are not specifically designed to check if your content is fully accessible, but they can provide a first level of verification, preview your content using test profiles.
t5: Use dark mode: Dark mode enhances visual accessibility for users with light sensitivity or visual impairments, for an improved viewing experience, provide accessible fallback styling if dark mode is not supported, finally, test all content and UI elements in both light and dark modes.
t6: Text for links and buttons links: Screen readers read out links using their text, if a link is labeled only _Click here_ or _Read more_ , users of assistive technologies don’t know the destination, to ensure accessibility, they need descriptive text that clearly indicates the target or action.
t7: Provide keyboard navigation and focus support keyboard: For landing pages, providing keyboard navigation and focus support allows people who cannot use a mouse to access and interact with content, it also improves overall usability by giving all users a clear and consistent way to move through information.

title: XDM Field Management | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition

title: Generative AI for content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Effective marketing objectives: When crafting marketing objectives, make sure they are clear, actionable, and measurable, avoid vague or generic statements, target IT directors at companies with 1000+ employees" Landing Pages "Convert B2B visitors into qualified leads by demonstrating how the enterprise security solution prevents 99.9% of cyber attacks, with Fortune 500 testimonials and free security audit".
t2: Communication strategy types: Your communication strategy determines how you present your message to maximize impact, different strategies work better for different goals, whether you are building urgency, establishing trust, or driving immediate action, choose the strategy that best aligns with your campaign objectives and audience mindset.
t3: Set the right tone tone: Tone shapes how your audience perceives and responds to your message, always select a tone that aligns with your brand voice and the stage of the profile journey, review the available tone options, including when each works best and examples of content that fit each style.

title: AI Assistant for Landing Page Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: (Beta) Select your Brand to ensure that the AI-generated content aligns with your brand specifications If there are no published brands, click Create a brand to define your reusable brand guidelines.
t2: In the Prompt field, enter a description of what you want to generate Use the Prompt Library if you need some help with crafting an effective prompt.
t3: Complete the content guidance settings to tailor the generated content: Text settings \- Provide guidance for the generated text content Image settings \- If you want to include images in the generated content, enable image generation and provide guidance.
t4: Scroll down in the AI Assistant panel and browse through the generated variations to determine which one is the best fit Click the _Full screen_ ( ) icon to open the _Generate Landing Page_ dialog If needed, use the refinement actions to fine-tune the variation to ensure that they meet your exact requirements.
t5: Click Select to replace the template contents with the selected variant and return to the landing page design space You can use the editing and formatting tools on the canvas to alter the generated content, as well as the _Settings_ and _Style_ options on the right.

title: Take an Action | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Account actions: In an account journey, use an action on accounts when you want to apply a change to all people that are part of accounts on the node path.
t2: Add an account-based action: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on a path and choose Take an action, in the node properties on the right, choose Accounts for the action, select an action from the list and set any values for the action.
t3: Activate to a LinkedIn destination: With the _Take an action_ node selected in the journey canvas, set the Action on accounts to Activate to destination, click Select destination, in the dialog, select the configured LinkedIn destination and click Save, enter the Audience name that is used to identify the activated audience in the destination.
t4: People actions: In an account or person journey, use an action on people when you want to apply a change to all people on the node path, for an account journey, this node type can be used within the _split path by people_ or _split path by accounts_.
t5: Add a people-based action: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on a path and choose Take an action, in the node properties on the right, choose People for the action, select an action from the list and set any values for the action.
t6: Journey Optimizer B2B actions: Choose Create new, click Create external customer audience, enter a Name (required) and Description (optional) for the new external audience, click Create, click Select external customer audience, in the dialog, select the audience that you want to use, click Add audience.

title: Role Insights Dashboard | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Filter the data: Click the _Filter_ ( ) icon at the top left to filter the displayed data using any of these attributes: Role \- Filters the data by one or more selected buying group roles.
t2: Engagement by role over time: This report tracks buying group activities over time, helping you to understand how recent campaigns drive engagement across different roles, use this information to optimize your marketing strategies and target specific roles more effectively.
t3: Drill through: For _Engagement by role_ , choose Drill through for an in-depth analysis of the engagements by role and solution interest, the global filters applied to the dashboard are carried over, click the _Filter_ ( ) icon at the top left to change the attribute filters for the drill-through view.
t4: View more: Choose View more to view extended data and insights, the displayed pop-up includes a chart and a table that show the breakdown of the data.

title: Listen for an Event | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click Edit event and define one or more web pages to match and any additional constraints for the event (Required) In the _Edit event_ dialog, define the Web page or Fills out form constraint.
t2: If needed, set the Timeout option to limit the time period to listen for the event (see Add a timeout to an event node).
t3: In a journey, add a _Listen for an event_ node, and select an Experience Platform event type for a people-based event _To include an Experience Event in your journey:_.
t4: Click Edit event and define one or more constraints for the event Click Add constraint and choose the field that you want to use for the constraint.
t5: Complete the remaining nodes for your journey and publish it When the journey is live (published) and reaches the _Listen for an event_ node, it begins listening for AEP Experience Events.

title: Split and Merge Paths | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the conditions editor, add one or more filters to define the split path Drag and drop filter attributes from the left navigation and complete the match definition.
t2: To add more paths, click Add path and repeat the previous steps to add conditions applicable to this path You can also label each path based on these conditions or use the default labels.
t3: Enable the Other accounts option to define the default path for accounts that are not a match for the defined segments/paths When this option is not enabled, the journey ends for accounts that do not match a defined segment/path within the split.
t4: Click Done when you have all conditions defined for the path For the identified accounts, you might then want to add an action node in the path to update the status of the buying group or stage, or to send a sales alert email.

title: LinkedIn Account Matched Audiences | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Enter the Account ID of your LinkedIn Campaign Manager Account You can find your Account ID by your Account Name in the Campaign Manager UI.
t2: Click Select buying group filters and define the parameters of your account audience note important At this time, filters cannot be edited after the dataflow is activated.
t3: Click Select LinkedIn destination and choose the configured LinkedIn destination that you want to use Upon activation, this setting creates the dataflow using the destination configuration and a corresponding virtual segment.
t4: Double-check your settings and click Activate at the top right Click Activate again in the confirmation dialog A banner is displayed with a link to your dataflows menu in Experience Platform so that you can check the dataflow record.
t5: From the node properties on the right, choose the destination If there are one or more destinations created, you can click Select destination to choose an existing destination.

title: Web channel configurations | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Enter a Name (required) and a Description (optional) for the configuration note Names must begin with a letter (A-Z) and can only contain alphanumeric characters.
t2: In the Web settings section, select one of the following options: Single page \- If you want to apply the changes to a single page only, enter or select a Page URL.
t3: If your use case requires multiple rules, click Add another page rule and repeat the previous step You can define up to 10 rules.
t4: Click the name of the duplicated web channel to edit the parameters Change the name and description to match the purpose or items in the rule.

title: Build and Publish a Journey | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Create a journey: Click Create Account Journey at the top-right of the page, in the dialog, enter a unique Name (required) and Description (optional), click Create, click Create Journey at the top-right of the page, in the dialog, enter a unique Name (required) and Description (optional), click Create.
t2: Building blocks for journey design: The _journey map_ is the central zone in the journey workspace, it is in this zone that you can add journey nodes and configure them, click a node to open its properties pane to the right of the canvas and set them according to your design.
t3: Guardrails: To help you build a journey without running into errors, the following guard rails are in place: _Deleting a Split path node_ : Deleting a node requires deleting all subsequent nodes in each path, _Deleting a Merge node_ : A merge node can be deleted only when there is one path connected to it.
t4: Add a node: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on the path and select the node type, set the node properties on the right.
t5: Delete a node: Navigate to the journey map, in the node properties on the right, click the _Delete_ ( ) icon, in the conformation dialog, click Delete.
t6: Add and delete a path: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on the path and add the split path node, in the node properties on the right, select Account, to add more paths, click Add path.
t7: Schedule a journey: Navigate to the journey map, schedule your journey by clicking Journey settings in the header, in the dialog, set the schedule options: Choose a schedule type, click Save.
t8: Publish a journey: At the top right of the journey map, click Publish, in the _Review journey settings_ dialog, set the journey start options, if needed, specify the End date for the journey, click Next, in the confirmation dialog, click Publish.

title: Structure Components | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: On the right panel with the _Styles_ tab selected, expand the Border section and set the options to display a border for the component.
t2: Move the toggle to the right to enable the border display options and set them according to your design criteria: To set the Border color , select the checkbox and click the color square to choose a color from the picker.
t3: For the Border radius , set the numerical value according to the curve you want for the corners A value of 0 (default) produces a squared corner.

title: Journey management | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click the _More_ icon (…) next to the journey name and choose Duplicate For all other journey statuses, click Duplicate at the top right.
t2: In the _Duplicate Journey_ dialog, set the Name and Description for the new journey By default, the dialog uses the name of the duplicated journey appended with __copy_.
t3: Choose the duplication Type : Partial content duplication \- Use this type to copy everything in the journey, excluding any created emails or SMS messages.

title: Solution Interests | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: From the _Solution interest_ tab, use one of the following methods to open the properties for the solution interest that you want to edit: Click the solution interest name.
t2: Make any needed updates to the solution interest settings: Update the Name and Description Select the Buying group stage model that is used for tracking buying group stage progression.
t3: From the _Solution interest_ tab, click the ellipsis (…) next to the solution interest and choose Delete This action opens a confirmation dialog If the solution interest is currently in use by an account journey or buying group job, the action results in an alert that it cannot be deleted.

title: Single-Page Applications | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Understanding SPAs: Unlike traditional multi-page websites where each navigation triggers a full page load, SPAs use JavaScript to update content dynamically while maintaining a single HTML page, this approach creates several considerations for web experiences: No page reloads \- Content changes occur without triggering traditional page load events.
t2: Configure SPA support: To personalize SPAs effectively, you need to configure view tracking so that Journey Optimizer B2B Edition can identify when users navigate between virtual views.
t3: Set up view declarations: Work with your development team to implement view declarations using the Adobe Web SDK, using these view declarations involve calling the sendEvent command with view information whenever the SPA navigates to a new view.
t4: Target specific views: In the web channel configuration, set up URL matching rules that align with your SPA routing structure, when creating modifications, specify the view where the modification should apply, use CSS selectors that target elements specific to each view.
t5: Handle dynamic content: In the non-visual editor, add a modification with a CSS selector, enable Wait for element and specify the maximum wait time, the modification applies once the target element appears in the DOM.
t6: SPA frameworks: Journey Optimizer B2B Edition web experiences work with popular SPA frameworks: Framework Considerations React Modifications apply after React renders components to the DOM, use class names or data attributes for targeting, angular Target elements after Angular’s change detection runs, avoid targeting elements with ngIf before they render.
t7: Use stable selectors: SPAs often generate dynamic class names or IDs (especially with CSS-in-JS solutions), as an alternative, you can use: Data attributes \- Add custom data attributes (data-testid, data-section, etc.) to elements you want to target, semantic HTML \- Target based on HTML structure and semantic elements.
t8: Test views: Navigate through all views where modifications apply, test the full user flow, including: Direct navigation to a view (deep linking) Navigation from other views within the SPA Browser backward and forward navigation, verify that modifications reapply when returning to a previously visited view.
t9: Handle view transitions: Some SPAs use animations or transitions between views, consider: Timing \- Ensure modifications apply after transition animations complete, element visibility \- Elements may exist but be hidden during transitions, flickering \- Apply modifications early enough to avoid visible content changes.
t10: Troubleshooting: Check view tracking \- Verify that sendEvent calls include the correct view name, verify element existence \- Ensure that target elements are in the DOM when modifications apply, review selectors \- Confirm CSS selectors match the actual DOM structure, check console \- Look for JavaScript errors that might prevent modifications.

title: Wait Nodes | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Add the wait node: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on a path and choose Wait, in the node properties on the right, set the Type of time to wait before the journey proceeds to the next node in the path.
t2: Advanced wait settings: Enable the Must end on option to configure an _advanced wait step_ and ensure that your messages reach people and account members at the optimal moment, this configuration gives you precise control over when a person or account exits a wait step and proceeds to the next node in the journey.
t3: Wait types: Wait type Description Configuration Specific time of day Hold until a specific time (such as 9:00 AM) Set the time (hour and minute), exits at the next occurrence of that time (for the selected time zone), specific day of week Hold until a particular day (such as Tuesday) Select a day of the week.
t4: Common scenarios: The following scenarios illustrate how you can apply typical scenarios to your wait node configuration: Email arrival during business hours Scenario: You market to B2B customers who read emails at work, you want all emails to arrive during business hours, solution: Configure your wait step to release leads at 9:00 AM on weekdays (Monday–Friday).

title: Helper functions | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Aggregation functions: Use aggregation functions to group multiple values to form a single summary value, you can also use array and list functions to define interactions with arrays, lists, and strings easier.
t2: Add add: Use the + (addition) function to find the sum of two argument expressions, syntax {%= double + double %} Example The following operation sums the price of two different products.
t3: And and: The and function is used to create a logical conjunction, syntax {%= query1 and query2 %} Example The following operation returns all people with home country (France) and birth year (1985).
t4: Or or: The or function is used to create a logical disjunction, syntax {%= query1 or query2 %} Example The following operation returns all people with home country (France) or birth year (1985).
t5: If (conditions): The if helper is used to define a conditional block, if the expression evaluation returns true, the block is rendered otherwise it is skipped, syntax {%#if contains(account.accountOrganization.primaryEmailDomain, ".edu")%} Following the if helper, you can enter an else statement to specify a block of code to be executed, if the same condition is false.
t6: Unless unless: Use the unless helper is to define a conditional block, by opposition to the if helper, if the expression evaluation returns false, the block is rendered.
t7: With with: Use the with helper to change the evaluation token of template-part, syntax The with helper is useful to define a shortcut variable too, example Use with for aliasing long variable names to shorter ones: Checkout our trending products for today!.
t8: Execution metadata: AVAILABILITY This capability is in Limited Availability, contact your Adobe representative to gain access, use the executionMetadata to capture and store custom key-value pairs dynamically into the message execution context, with this function, you can append contextual information to any native action from your campaigns or journeys.

title: Fragment Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.
t4: To edit the column properties, click the _Styles_ tab on the right and change them according to your needs: For Background , change the background color as needed.
t5: Click the Enable edition option toggle and set the editable fields Change the toggle to an enabled state for each field where you want to allow customization.

title: Buying Group Role Templates | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To filter the list by name, use the search field at the top of the list Enter the first few characters of the name to reduce the displayed list to the matching items.
t2: Click Add Condition and define the conditional rule for the role In the _Condition_ dialog, expand the list of Person attributes and locate an attribute that you want to use to match the role.
t3: For each additional role that you want to include for the template, click Add another role and repeat steps 1 and 2 to define the role.
t4: In the dialog, change the Members required value for each defined role as needed You can enter the value, or click + or − to increase or decrease the value.

title: Sales Qualifier | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In Header Parameters, set any HTTP headers that need to be send Generally, it is a JSON object that is sent and requires a content-type header.
t2: Set throttling and cache values in the Payload configuration section Click the pencil icon In the _Paste Payload_ dialog, paste or enter your JSON payload object.
t3: Click Test Connection to ensure that your settings are correct When the connection settings are valid, click Save as draft When you are back on the main _Integrations_ table, select the integration and click Activate to make the integration live.

title: Web Experience Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: With the _Content_ tab displayed in the web experience details page, click Edit web experience in the right panel The visual editor loads your website based on the web channel configuration.
t2: If needed, click Browse at the top right and use the site navigation bar to load the specific page that you want to modify.
t3: To define how you want the displayed page to be modified for the web experience, you can: Insert new components (divider, HTML, image, heading, paragraph, or link) to the page for the web experience.
t4: Repeat step 2 to load other pages that you want to include in the web experience and repeat step 3 to define the page modifications.
t5: (Optional) Enter new text for the button, or select the text string and enter your replacement text You can use personalization to alter the button text using data from account or person profiles.

title: Add Custom CSS for Your Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Add your custom CSS: With at least one content component added in the canvas, select the Body component in the left navigation, select the _Styles_ tab on the right and click Add custom CSS, enter your CSS code in the editor, click Save to save the custom CSS.
t2: CSS in imported content: If you want to use custom CSS with content imported into the email or landing page design space, consider the following: If you import external HTML content including CSS, it is populated in Compatibility mode and the CSS styles section is not available.
t3: Troubleshooting: If your custom CSS is not applied as expected, use the browser developer tools to inspect the content and verify that your CSS is targeting the correct selectors, as you review the styling code, consider the following: Check that your CSS is valid and free of syntax errors (such as missing braces, incorrect property names).

title: Web Experiences | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click Add to Chrome , and then click Add Extension in the confirmation dialog If you are using Microsoft Edge, this action adds the extension to Edge.
t2: In the _Create web experience_ dialog, enter a useful Name and Description (optional) Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters note Name and description fields support alpha, numeric, and special characters.
t3: Click the Actions tab and select the Web channel to use for the web experience The web channel configuration determines where the content modifications are applied based on the configured page matching rules.
t4: In the right panel, set the web experience properties according to how you want to define and manage it Visual editor \- Toggle between the visual and non-visual editor for the web experience modification design.
t5: When the modifications are complete, click the left arrow above the editor to return to the content tab and personalized web experience node properties.
t6: Select the Content tab and use the visual design tools as needed _Visual editor_ \- Click Edit Content _Non-visual editor_ \- Click Add a modification.

title: Content Components | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the Components library, grab the _Drag handle_ for the content component of your choice, then drag and drop it onto the structure components.
t2: On the right panel with the _Styles_ tab selected, expand the Border section and set the options to display a border for the component.
t3: Move the toggle to the right to enable the border display options and set them according to your design criteria: To set the Border color , select the checkbox and click the color square to choose a color from the picker.
t4: For the Border radius , set the numerical value according to the curve you want for the corners A value of 0 (default) produces a squared corner.
t5: Set the Type for the link: External link \- Choose this type to use a standard URL as the link destination In Url , enter the URL for the link destination.
t6: For Label , enter the text that you want to display inside the button The button sizing adjusts according to the text and the styling that set.

title: Fragments | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create fragment_ dialog, enter a useful Name and Description (optional) Fragment requirements: Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters Alpha, numeric, and special characters are allowed Reserved characters are _not allowed_ : \ / : ?.
t2: Use the content design tools to create the visual fragment content: Add structure and content Add Assets Navigate the layers, settings, and styles Personalize content Enable custom fields Edit linked URL tracking.
t3: (Optional) Apply a brand theme to the fragment content to streamline the fragment authoring process and make sure that the design aligns with defined standards.
t4: From the _Fragments_ listing page, click the fragment name to open it A preview of the visual content is displayed, with the fragment details on the right.
t5: To make changes to the content in the visual design space, click Edit fragment Use the visual design tools as needed: Add structure and content Add Assets Navigate the layers, settings, and styles Personalize content Enable custom fields Edit linked URL tracking Click Save , or Save & close to return to the fragment details.
t6: When the fragment meets your criteria and you want to make it available for use in an email or email template, click Publish Published.

title: Account Lists | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Add accounts by filter_ dialog, use the Account Filters menu to add the attributes and activities that you want to use to construct the filter set: The filters are nested into category folders.
t2: When the filter set and logic are complete, click Populate accounts The population process may take some time, depending on the number of accounts to evaluate and populate (the size of your database and the filter criteria you selected).
t3: In the _Publish static account list_ dialog, click Publish to confirm Dynamic account list You can proceed to publish a dynamic account list as soon as the filter set is complete.

title: Content personalization | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Personalization tokens: In Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, you can build your dynamic email content using personalization tokens: Account tokens \- These tokens are based on the account attributes, such as _account name_ , _industry_ , and _number of employees_.
t2: Personalization editor: The personalization editor is available in every context where you need to define personalization in email content, in the editor, you can select, arrange, customize, and validate all the data to create a customized personalization for your content, add personalization in any field or content component by clicking the _Add personalization_ ( ) icon.
t3: Tokens and helper functions: To use a personalization token or helper function, locate it in the left navigation pane and click + to add it to the expression.
t4: Custom datasets: Beta You can use relational schemas for email personalization, the custom objects are defined within _relational schemas_ , and a product administrator can configure relational schema fields in Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, these fields are accessible in the personalization editor.

title: Email Template Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t4: To open the fragments listing, select the _Fragments_ icon ( ) You can: Sort the listing Browse, search, or filter the listing Switch between thumbnail and list views.
t5: Drag and drop any of the fragments into the structural component The editor renders the fragment within the section/element of the email structure note tip To add the fragment so that it occupies the entire horizontal layout within the email, add a 1:1 column structure and then drag and drop the fragment into it.
t6: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.

title: Create Brands for Content Generation and Consistency | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Access your brand library: To access brands kits in Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, go to the left navigation and click Content Management > Brands, this action opens a page where the created brands are displayed as cards.
t2: Brand management actions: For each card, you can click the _More menu_ ( ) icon and choose an action for the brand: View brand \- Open the brand page and display the definitions, mark as default brand (Live only) - Mark the brand as the default for content alignment and generation.
t3: Create and define a brand: To create and define your brand guidelines, you can either enter the details or upload your brand guideline documents to use for automatic extraction.
t4: Add the brand: At the top-right of the _Brands_ page, click Create brand, enter a Name for your brand, drag and drop or select your file to upload your brand guidelines and extract automatically relevant brand information, click Create brand.
t5: Refine and update the brand guidelines: Browse through the different tabs to adapt and define more detailed information as needed, in each details tab, review the categories and improve the brand by adding, removing, and changing your definitions, when you have everything defined, click Save.
t6: Publish the brand: When your brand includes a complete set of definitions and meets your requirements, click Publish to make your brand guidelines available for content alignment and generation, published brands are accessible from the Brand option in the AI brand alignment score and content generation tools.
t7: Writing style: The _Writing style_ definitions outline the standards for writing content, and details how language, formatting, and structure should be used to maintain clarity, coherence, and consistency across all materials, select the Writing Style tab, and review each category, do not be defeatist, writing Mechanics Keep sentences short and impactful.
t8: Visual content: The _Visual content_ definitions outline the standards for imagery and design, and detail the specifications needed to maintain a unified and consistent brand look, select the Visual content tab, and review each category, avoid overly edited or pixelated images, illustration standards Use clean, minimalistic styles.
t9: Edit a published brand: Open the brand page and click Edit brand at the top right, in the confirmation dialog, click Edit Brand, browse through the different tabs to update the brand information as needed, click Save as you work with the draft updates, and then Publish when you are ready to replace the _Live_ version.

title: Use Account Lists in Journeys and Programs | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Account audience node: Select the Account list option for the starting _Account audience_ node, click Add accounts list, select the checkbox for the account list and click Save.
t2: Take an action node - Add to account: Select the _Action on_ Accounts option, for _Action on accounts_ , choose Add to account list, for Select live static account list , choose the account list where you want to add accounts.
t3: Take an action node - Remove from account: Select the _Action on_ Accounts option, for _Action on accounts_ , choose Remove from account list, for Select live static account list , choose the account list where you want to remove accounts.
t4: Add the filter to a Smart List: In Marketo Engage, select a campaign and click the Smart List tab, in the filters list displayed on the right, enter Member and locate the Member of Account List filter, drag the filter onto the Smart List canvas.
t5: Review the members: After the flow runs, you can view the list of people populated in the list, open the list and select the People tab.

title: Email Templates | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create email_ dialog, choose the type of email content that you want to use for the template Use Themes \- Choose this option to create the email template in _Theme mode_.
t2: Drag and drop the HTML or .zip file containing your HTML content and click Import You can personalize the imported content as needed in the visual design space.
t3: Access the visual design space from the _Edit content_ page On the _Create your email_ page, the _Sample templates_ tab is selected by default.
t4: To use a custom email template, select the Saved templates tab This tab displays a list of all email templates created on the sandbox.

title: Configure Engagement Score Weighting | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click Engagement score weighting on the intermediate panel to display the list of scoring models From this page, you can create (duplicate), activate, and edit engagement score models.
t2: In the _Duplicate_ dialog, enter a unique name for the duplicated model and click Duplicate Click the name to open the score model details and make your changes.
t3: For each weight band, adjust the name or values according to your needs: Change the name in the _Weighting band_ field Enter a new value.
t4: If needed, add another weighting band: Click \+ Add weighting band at the bottom of the list This action inserts a blank weighting band at the bottom of the list.

title: In-CRM Insights | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Set permissions: Create a custom role and assign it the Sales Insights: View Sales Insights permission, create a new user group, add an Experience Platform product profile to the group.
t2: Install the package: Download the In-CRM Insights installer package, after sign-in, you are redirected to the package installation page, select the Install for All Users option and click Install, approve third-party access in the dialog, then click Continue, when the installation finishes, click Done, download the In-CRM Insights installer package, go to the Power Apps porta.
t3: View your buying groups: Follow the prompts to log in to your Adobe account, your buying groups are loaded and available to view, after selecting a buying group, you can browse the group details, this is the same as the data and insights displayed in Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, but data is read-only through In-CRM Insights.

title: Forms | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create form_ dialog, enter a useful Name (required) and Description (optional) Form requirements: Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters Alpha, numeric, and special characters are allowed Reserved characters are _not allowed_ : \ / : ?.
t2: From the _Forms_ list page, click the form name to open it A preview of the form content is displayed, with the form details on the right.
t3: To make changes to the form in the visual design space, click Edit form Use the visual design tools as needed: Add fields Change field styling Reorder fields Change submit button text and styling Change the form styling Click Save & close to return to the form details.
t4: When the form meets your criteria and you want to make it available for use in a landing page or landing page template, click Publish.
t5: Use the visual design tools as needed to update the form content: Add fields Change field styling Reorder fields Change submit button text and styling Change the form styling Click Save & close to return to the form details.

title: Use AI Assistant | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Ask product knowledge questions: Product knowledge questions are about Journey Optimizer B2B Edition concepts and how-to information, some examples of product knowledge questions include: How do I set up SMS provider accounts?, how do I send an email in a journey?, how can I personalize my email content?.
t2: Product knowledge sources: After receiving a response for a product question, select Show source to view the product knowledge source citations used to generate the AI Assistant response, aI Assistant provides links to the documentation that corroborates the initial response.
t3: Operational insights sources: After receiving a response for an operational insights question, click Show source and then select View source query, you can verify each response related to operational insights questions using an SQL query that AI Assistant provides.
t4: Provide feedback: Use the _Thumb up_ ( ) or _Thumb down_ ( ) icons to rate the usefulness and quality of the response, complete the brief survey form according to your experience and click Submit, the information that you provide is used to make improvements to AI Assistant.

title: Landing Page Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t4: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.
t5: To edit the column properties, click the _Styles_ tab on the right and change them according to your needs: For Background , change the background color as needed.

title: Use Brand Themes for Email Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Access the theme tools using one of the following methods: Create a new email template and click Edit email template to launch the _Design your template_ page.
t2: Select the default theme, or use any of the Adobe themes to use as the starting point note If you want to use one of your custom themes (_My themes_) as a starting point, you can duplicate it and change the theme name when you edit the theme.
t3: Use the right navigation to access the different theme style tabs and change the theme settings: General settings Colors Text settings Spacing and border Button Divider Grid The visual elements change on the canvas as you define the new theme settings.
t4: Click Close to return to the _Create a theme_ page, and then Cancel to return to the design page You can then choose Design from scratch to open the visual design space and use the theme for the email or template.
t5: Select one of the following actions: Select an email template that incorporates a theme (created in _Theme mode_) The theme that is specific to each template is automatically applied.
t6: In the email design space, click the _Themes_ ( ) icon on the right You can switch between the color variants for this theme.

title: Custom Tokens for Email Personalization | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _My Tokens_ page, click Create and choose the token type that you want to define: Text \- Use this type to define a token with a basic text string value.
t2: In the dialog, enter the Name and Value for the token You can use _camel case_ , such as EventType, to use a multi-word name that is easily identified.
t3: Select the text component and click the _Add personalization_ ( ) icon in the toolbar The dialog includes a _My tokens_ folder in the _Personalization Tokens_ library if there are custom tokens defined for the account journey.
t4: Expand the My tokens folder, then click + or … to add one of your custom tokens to the blank space You can add any additional static text as needed.

title: Email Collaboration Tools | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Enable email collaboration tools for reviewers: In the Permissions app, go to the Roles tab and select the desired role, click Edit to modify the permissions, add the B2B Assets resource, then select Manage B2B Emails, click Save to apply the changes.
t2: Display collaboration tools and comments: While creating, editing, or reviewing content in the email design space, you can access the _Collaboration_ panel to add or manage comments for the email content, click the _Collaboration_ ( ) icon in the right navigation.
t3: Collaboration workflow: Invite your collaborators and reviewers, reviewers add comments, read comments, add replies to discuss feedback, and make needed edits, reviewers or authors resolve comments.
t4: Invite collaborators and reviewers: Select the body of the email, click the _Collaboration_ ( ) icon in the right navigation, at the top of the right panel, enter your invitation text for users to collaborate and provide feedback, click Submit.
t5: Add comments: Select a structure or content component, in the toolbar, click the _Collaboration_ tool, enter your comment in the text field, click Submit.
t6: Resolve comments: As an author or designer, assess the feedback from reviewers and determine what changes that you want to make, when changes are complete and the request is satisfied, click the _More menu_ ( … ) icon and choose Resolve.
t7: Place a comment: If a comment is not associated with an element on the email canvas, you can _pin_ the comment to an element as needed, click the _More menu_ ( … ) icon and choose Place the comment, then, select the design component on the canvas.
t8: Remove or delete comments: You can clean up your comments log by removing and deleting them, click the _More menu_ ( … ) icon and choose Remove Comment or Delete, the comment is still part of the comment record for the email, when you delete a comment, the action permanently deletes it from the record.
t9: Resolved comments: By default, resolved comments are hidden in the _Collaboration_ panel, you can display resolved comments at any time by clearing the filter, click the _Filter_ ( ) icon and clear the Hide resolved comments checkbox.

title: In-CRM access to detail pages | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click New to create a formula (text) field, and add it to an _Account_ , _Contact_ , or _Lead_ layout For the formula, use the following examples as a guide.
t2: Click New Button or Link in the top-right corner and create the detail page link For the formula, use the following examples as a guide.
t3: In the ribbon at the top of the page, click Save and then Publish 3 - Add the JS web resource to the form libraries.
t4: On the _Home_ tab at the top, click Save and then Publish 4 - Verify the link To verify the link, check the Account, Contact, or Lead view in Dynamics.
t5: On the HOME tab for the Account, Contact, or Lead form, select Body (to create the linked resource in the _Summary_ section) or Header (to create it in the header menu).

title: Adobe Target External Audiences | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: From the node properties on the right, set the external audience If there are one or more external audiences already created, you can choose Select existing and select the audience that you want to use.
t2: In the _Add audience_ dialog, select the audience that you want to use You can enter text in the _Search_ field to filter the displayed items for a match of the audience name.
t3: Locate the destination connection that you want to use to activate your segments, click the _More menu_ ( … ) icon next to the name, and choose Activate audiences.

title: Buying Groups | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Key components: You can increase marketing effectiveness by establishing buying groups that identify members for your target account lists for the solutions that your Sales teams are responsible for selling, before you and your Marketing team starts creating your buying groups, make sure that you have the key components defined.
t2: Member assignment: _Manual action_ \- A manual add member or remove member action performed by a sales user for the buying group, _Journey action_ \- Journey action nodes for buying group membership (_Assign to Buying group_ or _Remove from Buying group_), _System jobs_ \- Buying group creation and maintenance jobs.
t3: Buying group workflow: Create buying groups, identify missing people by completeness, complete the buying groups definitions, add buying group actions to your account journeys.
t4: View buying groups and components: On the left navigation, expand Accounts and click Buying groups, the _Buying groups_ page is organized as tabs: Tab Description Overview This tab is the default and displays the Buying groups dashboard, browse This tab supports the following activities: View the list of existing buying groups.
t5: Buying group engagement score: The engagement score is based on the buying group member activities, weighted actions, and weighted roles, the resulting score is normalized within the tenant/instance to enable consistent comparison and allow for actionable insights, the initial engagement score calculation starts as soon as you create the buying group and is re-calculated daily.

title: Preview and test your email content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Simulate_ page, select a person profile in the People list to use for rendering the email In the content preview, personalized elements are populated according to the selected person profile.
t2: For each additional recipient that you want to include in the review, click Add recipient and enter their email address in the Send to field.
t3: In the _Add people for testing_ dialog, enter the full email address for the contact To add multiple contacts, enter multiple addresses separated by a comma.

title: Test Email Rendering | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click Connect to confirm the connection between Litmus and Journey Optimizer B2B Edition and send the email content for rendering note important When you connect your Litmus account with Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, you agree that test messages are sent to Litmus.
t2: Check your email content in popular desktop, mobile and web-based clients Click the displayed thumbnail to view the details for any of the rendered client tests.
t3: When you are finished reviewing, click the back arrow ( ) at the top-left to return to the Simulate content page You can select another profile and do another rendering test, or return to the email design space to make any needed adjustments based on your review.

title: Landing Pages | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create landing page_ dialog, enter a useful Name and Description (optional) Landing page requirements: Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters Alpha, numeric, and special characters are allowed Reserved characters are _not allowed_ : \ / : ?.
t2: Drag and drop the HTML or .zip file containing your HTML content and click Import You can personalize the imported content as needed with the visual design space.
t3: From the _Landing pages_ listing page, click the landing page name to open it A preview of the visual content is displayed, with the landing page details on the right.
t4: To make changes to the content in the visual design space, click Edit landing page Use the visual design tools as needed: Add structure and content Add Assets Navigate the layers, settings, and styles Personalize content Edit linked URL tracking.
t5: From the _Landing page_ listing page, click the page name to open it A preview of the visual content is displayed, with the landing page details on the right.
t6: If you want to update the content, click Edit landing page on the right Click Create draft version in the dialog to open the draft version in the visual design space.

title: Edit Images with Adobe Express | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: When you return to the main Adobe Express quick actions editor, click Save to save the modified image file in the Journey Optimizer B2B Edition asset repository using the same file name.
t2: Use the resize settings to reduce or expand the image: Select an Aspect ratio option Use a standard size for digital content or choose Custom if you want to enter values for Width and Height to meet your needs.
t3: Drag the handles on the corners of the image to remove the outer areas that you do not want to include in the image asset.

title: Buying Group Details | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Members tab: Select the Members tab to view a list of all buying group members, each member listing includes the name, role, job title, email address, phone number, and source.
t2: Assign a new member: Click Assign new member at the top-right, in the _Assign member_ dialog, select the account leads that you want to add to the buying group and click Next, in the _Edit new member role_ dialog, select the role to assign to each of the new members, click Save.
t3: Remove a member: Select the checkboxes for the members that you want to remove, in the selection bar at the bottom, click Remove members, in the confirmation dialog, click Remove.
t4: Edit role: Select the checkboxes for the members that you want to change roles, in the selection bar at the bottom, click Edit roles, in the _Edit member role_ dialog, select the role to assign to each of the members, click Save.
t5: Send email: Select the checkboxes for the members that you want to receive the email, at the top-right or in the selection bar at the bottom, click Send email, in the _Send email_ dialog, select the Marketo Engage workspace, and then select the checkbox for the email that you want to send, click Send.

title: Journey Agent B2B | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Basic usage: To use the Journey Agent Build skill, type into the prompt window what you are looking to create, using natural language: “Create a B2B journey to invite decision makers to a roadshow in engaged accounts most likely to open new pipeline.” The more detail that you can provide, the better the reply will be.
t2: End-to-end B2B journey creation: The Journey Build skill can generate an end-to-end journey flow (account or person journey) from natural language text prompts and metadata, through a conversational experience rather than a traditional user interface.
t3: Multi-stage journeys: You can act as a B2B journey designer to create a multi-stage customer account journey that informs decision-makers and marketing personas early in the exploration phase, the goal is to convert anonymous visitors into known contacts, deepen engagement with relevant content, and prime qualified leads for sales outreach.
t4: Journey lifecycle and timing: Retrieve key timestamps for a journey or specific accounts: “When did this journey go live?” “When did the first account enter this journey?” “When did account QiDemoAccount50 start this journey?”.

title: Work with Internal Image Assets | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Add assets_ dialog, drag and drop one or more files from your system to the file box You can upload assets from your local system of up to 10 files at a time.
t2: In the dialog, enter the folder name and select the destination (parent) folder for the new folder Folder names must be unique, with a maximum of 100 characters, and cannot contain special characters, such as ;, :, \, |.
t3: In the _Add assets_ dialog, drag and drop the files from your system You can also click the link to use your file system to select the files.

title: Email Content Creation with GenStudio for Performance Marketing | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: GenStudio content generation capabilities: Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing is a generative AI-first application that empowers marketing teams to create impactful, personalized ads and emails that adhere to brand standards and comply with their enterprise policies.
t2: Export HTML from Journey Optimizer B2B Edition: In Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, access the content of your email in the visual design space, from the _More …_ menu at the top of the email design space, choose Export HTML.
t3: Use the exported HTML in GenStudio for Performance Marketing: GenStudio for Performance Marketing recognizes certain elements within the imported email HTML when they are identified with a recognized field name, add field names in the exported HTML using the Handlebars syntax where you need GenStudio for Performance Marketing to generate a certain type of content.
t4: Create the template: Use the HTML file to create a template in GenStudio for Performance Marketing, for detailed information about uploading an HTML template into GenStudio in the Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing, refer to Add a template in the GenStudio for Performance Marketing documentation.
t5: Generate email experiences: In GenStudio for Performance Marketing, use the template to create several email experience variations and save them, for detailed information about generating branded email experiences, refer to Create an email experience in the GenStudio for Performance Marketing.
t6: Add generated email experiences to Journey Optimizer B2B Edition: In Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, add an email to an account journey using a _Take an action_ node, on the _Create your Email_ page, select Import HTML, in the _Import your email_ dialog, click Adobe GenStudio for Performance Marketing, browse the published experiences.

title: Form Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Fields: Form fields are used to capture person profile data that can be used to target people and associate them with accounts and buying groups.
t2: Add a field: In the _Components_ panel on the left, drag the Field content component and drop it onto the canvas, click Select field attribute, in the _Select field attribute_ dialog, select the checkbox for the person profile attribute that you want to use for the field and click Select, if needed, change the Label text.
t3: Change field styling: Select the Styles tab in the right panel to change the styling for the selected field, background \- Select the checkbox to apply a background color for the field, white is the default color, click the Background color square to open the popup color picker and choose a color for the field background.
t4: Reorder fields: You can move form fields directly in the visual workspace, click the _Move_ tool on the right edge of the selected field and drag it to a new location, add structural components to the form and move fields into columns to group them and change the layout.
t5: Delete or duplicate a field: Click the _Delete_ icon ( ) in the toolbar or the right panel to delete a selected field, in the confirmation dialog, click Delete, click the _Duplicate_ icon ( ) in the toolbar or the right panel to duplicate a selected field.
t6: Submit button: The submit button (footer field) is part of the form by default and cannot be removed, select the butto/footer component in the form to change the text and styling for the button.
t7: Style the submit button: Select the Styles tab in the right panel to change the styling for the selected button/footer component, background \- Select the checkbox to apply a background color for the button, blue is the default color.
t8: Form styling: You can change styles for the form area when you click outside of the structural or form components, the form components (fields and button) inherit the _Body_ styles defined the top-level styles, unless other styles are defined at the field or button/footer level.
t9: CSS styles: Click View CSS in the right panel to review the CSS code, select the CSS code in the scrolling window and copy it to your clipboard, click Close, (Optional) Paste the copied code into your favorite CSS tool and edit the CSS to reflect the styling that you want.
t10: Manual styling: Change the settings in the right panel to define the display for the whole form, background color \- Select the checkbox to apply a background color around the form area, white is the default color, click the color square to open the popup color picker and choose a color for the form background.

title: Dark Mode for Email Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: For the images and icons, define specific assets for dark mode only You cannot change the colors of images and icons, but you can define alternative assets to be used for dark mode.
t2: At any point during your design changes, select Switch to live view to check how your content might render on various device sizes From this view, change the selector to _Dark mode_ ( ) to preview the dark mode version of your content across the different devices.
t3: If you have a Litmus Enterprise account, select Render email to see the final dark mode rendering for various email clients in the Litmus integration.

title: Landing Page Template Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t4: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.
t5: To edit the column properties, click the _Styles_ tab on the right and change them according to your needs: For Background , change the background color as needed.

title: Persona Mapping | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Access the configured personas: In the left navigation, choose Administration > Configurations, click Persona mapping on the intermediate panel to display the list of personas, to access the details for a persona, click the name.
t2: Create a persona: In the left navigation, choose Administration > Configuration, click Persona mapping in the intermediate panel, click Create persona, enter a unique Name and Description (optional) for the persona, select the attributes to use for matching the persona, for each attribute, enter the comma-separated values that you want to match for the attribute.
t3: Edit a persona: Click the persona name to access and edit the details for the persona, You can change the name or description, add attributes, or update the attribute values, click Submit when your changes are complete.
t4: Delete a persona: On the _Persona mapping_ page, locate the persona that you want to delete, next to the name, click the ellipses (…) icon for and choose Delete, in the confirmation dialog, click Delete.

title: Configure Experience Manager Asset Repositories | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Add a repository connection: In the left navigation, choose Administration > Configuration, click Assets on the intermediate panel, within the _Adobe Experience Manager Assets_ box, click the arrow next to Configure a repository and choose the repository, click Add a certificate and use the dialog tools to upload the file.
t2: Replace a certificate: On the digital asset management page, locate the list of the configured repositories, click the desired repository to replace the certificate, click the ellipses (…) icon for the certificate file to reveal the options for actions on it, choose Replace to open the dialog for file upload.
t3: View a certificate: On the digital asset management page, locate the list of the configured repositories, click the connected repository, click the ellipses (…) icon for the certificate file to reveal the options for actions on it, choose View, click Close to return to the Configure repository page.
t4: Delete a repository connection: On the _Digital asset management_ page, locate the list of the configured asset repositories, click the desired repository name to edit the connection, click the ellipses (…) icon for the certificate file to reveal the options for actions on it, choose Delete, in the confirmation dialog, click Delete.

title: Create Buying Groups | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Guidance page: The first page provides guidance about the prerequisites/components that are required for creating buying groups, if you know that you have the necessary components in place, click Next.
t2: Components: Select each component that you want to use: Solution interest \- Select the solution interest from the list, after you select the solution interest and the account audience, click Create.
t3: Confirmation: The confirmation dialog provides a summary of the buying groups process and an estimated time for completion, to confirm and launch the process, click Create.
t4: Buying group creation jobs: The creation job automatically creates buying groups for each new account in the account audience, you can navigate to the _Solution interest_ tab, which displays the count of creation jobs created for each solution interest, click the number in the Buying group creation jobs column to view the list of creation jobs.

title: Intent Data | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Prepare your intent mapping data: In the left navigation, choose Administration > Configuration, click Intent Mapping in the intermediate panel, click Create category, in the dialog, click the Download file template link, click Cancel, use the template to define your intent mapping data: Rename the file to reflect your category name, such as _Personalization at scale_.
t2: Upload a category file: Click Create category, drag and drop the file into the _Upload files_ dialog, or click Select a file to locate and select the file on your system, click Next.
t3: Approve or reject the category: Review the category listing and click Approve to activate the keywords for use in the Intelligent Dashboard, Account details page, Buying group details page, and Person details page, click View all to display the full list for each product, or click Download to review the full list as an Excel file.

title: Add an Email to Your Journey | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Add an email action node in a journey: For the _Action on_ target, choose People, for the _Action on people_ , choose Send email, for the _Email source_ , choose how you want to source the email to send.
t2: Define the email settings: With the Details tab selected in the _Summary_ panel on the right, scroll to the bottom to view and define the email settings, enter the name of the sender as you want it to appear to the recipient, click the _Personalize_ icon ( ) to use a personalization token in the field.
t3: Check alerts: As you design your email message content, alerts are displayed in the interface (top-right of the page) when key settings are missing, if you do not see this button, there are no detected issues, note Marketing-style email messages must include an opt-out link, which is not required for transactional messages.

title: Buying Group Stages | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Define the first stage by entering the Name (required) and Description (optional) You designate the entry stage and the flow between stages when you define the transition rules.
t2: When you are satisfied with the stages that you have defined, click Save note important After the buying group stages are saved, they cannot be removed. However, you can change the name and description for any of the stages as long as the model remains in _Draft_ status.
t3: For each non-destination stage, define one or more stages that come next in the flow (transition) All non-destination stages must have at least one Allowed transit to stage selected.
t4: When you are satisfied with the transition rules that are defined, click Save You can also click _Cancel_ to close the dialog and return to the model details page without any changes.
t5: Open the solution interest using one of the following methods to open the properties for the solution interest that you want to edit: Click the solution interest name.

title: Conditional Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar The component is outlined in orange to indicate that it is activated as a conditional component.
t2: Hover over the first variant (_Variant - 1_) and click the _Select condition_ icon ( ) If you want to view details for a condition to ensure it is what you want, click the _More menu_ icon (…) and choose View Info.
t3: Select the conditional rule and click Select to associate it with the variant You can review the associated condition by clicking the _More menu_ icon (…) for the variant and choosing View condition.
t4: For better readability, rename the variant by clicking the _More menu_ icon (…) for the variant and choosing Rename Enter a meaningful name for the variant that helps you to identify the variant and its intent.
t5: In the _Select condition_ dialog, click Create new and choose the condition type: Person condition \- Choose this type to build the conditional rule using person attributes and contextual events.
t6: On the right, enter the Name and a Description (optional) for the rule Use a meaningful name and useful description to help others in your organization so that they can reuse it instead of creating another duplicate condition.

title: Assets | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Asset management: If you are provisioned with Adobe Experience Manager as a Cloud Services and it is configured as an asset source in Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, you have access to both repository types when your user account has the required permissions, these repositories are separate and not in sync.
t2: Internal assets: The internal assets repository is provided by default with every Journey Optimizer B2B Edition subscription, this means that you have access to any of the image assets stored in the connected Adobe Marketo Engage asset file system, you can use this repository as your local assets library, including upload and download assets functions.
t3: Adobe Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service: Bring marketing and creative workflows together using Adobe Experience Manager Assets, it is natively integrated with Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, so you can easily access Assets as a Cloud Service to discover and use digital assets.
t4: Use assets for content authoring: Use assets as you author your emails, email templates, and visual fragments, the visual content editor provides access to the images in your connected asset repositories, if you also have a subscription for Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service, you can choose image assets from either source.

title: Intelligent Dashboard | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Buying group stages: The _Buying Group Stages_ chart provides an overview of buying group progression across different stages (based on transition rules set up by an administrator), availability of buying group stages requires configuration of the buying group stages.
t2: Time period: Use the date filter at the top right to change the date range for the data visualizations, click the down arrow to set a relative date range, or to set custom start and end dates.
t3: Attribute filter: Click the _Filter_ ( ) icon at the top left to filter the data display using any of these attributes: Solution Interest Account Stage name.

title: SMS Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click the _Personalize_ icon ( ) to the right of the text message box The dialog provides access to the account tokens, person tokens, and system tokens.
t2: Add a token by clicking the plus ( + ) symbol next to it If you want to add the token with a fallback (default that appears in case that field is not available for a lead), click the _More_ icon ( … ) and choose Insert with fallback text.
t3: When your personalization tokens are placed, click Save to save changes and return to the main SMS authoring workspace You can continue to edit the message with the tokens as needed.
t4: If you choose to use a Marketo Engage landing page, set the tracking options Enable tracking \- Select this checkbox to enable tracking, which requires _shortening_ the URL.
t5: In the _SMS properties_ section, enter a Name (required, 100 character maximum) and Description (optional, 300 character maximum) for your message Alpha, numeric, special characters are allowed for these fields.
t6: Choose the SMS Type : Use Marketing for promotional text messages, which require user consent Use Transactional for non-commercial messages, such as order confirmation, password reset notifications, or delivery information.

title: Email Message Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create email_ dialog, choose the type of email content that you want to author Use Themes \- Choose this option to create the email in _Theme mode_.
t2: Drag and drop the HTML or .zip file containing your HTML content and click Import You can personalize the imported content as needed with the visual email editor tools.
t3: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t4: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t5: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t6: To open the fragments listing, select the _Fragments_ icon ( ) You can: Sort the listing Browse, search, or filter the listing Switch between thumbnail and list views.

title: SMS Channel Configurations | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: If needed, click the _Filter_ icon ( ) and select options to display the list of configured API credentials by the SMS service provider or creator.
t2: Click Submit when the configuration details of your API credentials are complete Twilio _To configure Twilio as your SMS provider with Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition:_.
t3: Click Submit at the top-right of the page when the configuration details of your API credentials are complete Infobip _To configure Infobip as your SMS provider with Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition:_.

title: AI Assistant for Email Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: (Required) In the Prompt field, enter a description of what you want to generate Use the Prompt Library if you need some help with crafting an effective prompt.
t2: Scroll the AI Assistant panel and browse through the generated variations to determine which one is the best fit You can submit feedback for a generated variant by clicking the _Thumbs Up_ , _Thumbs Down_ , or _Flag_ icon and choose the reason that best summarizes your feedback.
t3: Click the Refine option to access additional customization features: Rephrase \- Rewrite the message while preserving its meaning This option helps you generate alternative wording or adjust phrasing without changing the core message.
t4: Click Select to replace the subject line text with the selected variant and return to the email properties Preheader generation An email preheader is the short summary text that follows the subject line when an email is viewed in the inbox.

title: Buying Groups Overview Dashboard | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition

t2: Drill through: Choose Drill through for an in-depth analysis of individual group scores or distributions, click the _Filter_ ( ) icon at the top left to change the attribute filters for the drill-through view, you can click the _More_ (…) menu at the top-right and choose View more to view extended data.
